title: map_board_destroy bad-frees district names + attribution: strings_clone allocates with the loader's allocator param, delete() frees with context.allocator
evidence: core/map.odin:320 `append(&b.districts, Map_District{name = strings_clone(name, allocator), kind = kind, pos = {f32(px), f32(py)}})` and :287 `b.attribution = strings_clone(attr, allocator)` vs the destroy `for d in b.districts {` / `delete(d.name)` (line 136) / `delete(b.attribution)` (line 139). `odin test core` tracking-allocator output: `+++ bad free        @ 0x50A802086 [map.odin:136:map_board_destroy()]` (fires because every loader test calls `map_board_load(transmute([]u8)src, &bal, context.temp_allocator)` — map_test.odin:105).
detail: Strings carry no allocator, so delete(d.name)/delete(b.attribution) free with context.allocator while the bytes were cloned with the board's allocator param. Any caller whose load allocator differs (all loader tests use context.temp_allocator) hits a bad free — heap-corruption UB without the tracking allocator. Violates the ODN-18 arena-discipline convention; the r1-W4 destroy fix is itself defective.
recommended_fix: Free with the same allocator that cloned: store the board allocator on Map_Board at load and use `delete(d.name, b.allocator)` / `delete(b.attribution, b.allocator)` in map_board_destroy.

title: ring_scratch in growth_plan_demand leaks one heap array per board-run growth window; the 'rides the caller's TEMP arena' comment is false
evidence: `// v2-dublin-board: the attach ring scratch — the board's ring scan fills it; the per-attempt draw indexes it. Rides the caller's TEMP arena (the same lifetime as the roster/gview scratch — freed by the frame's free_all, never owned).` / `ring_scratch: [dynamic]u32` (line 711). grep shows ring_scratch referenced only at lines 711, 815, 820 — never deleted. `odin test core` output under `core.test_growth_dublin_attach_stays_in_estate_radius`: `+++ leak        32B @ 0x655004E60 [growth.odin:526:growth_board_ring_scan()]`.
detail: A zero-value [dynamic]u32 appends via context.allocator, not context.temp_allocator, and nothing deletes it — one leaked backing array per ATTACH-bearing growth window on dublin runs (unbounded with session length). Violates the ODN-18 arena discipline the comment claims to follow; proven leaking by the project's own tracking allocator.
recommended_fix: Allocate the scratch explicitly from the temp arena (`ring_scratch = make([dynamic]u32, 0, 0, context.temp_allocator)`) or add `defer delete(ring_scratch)`.

title: dublin_board.dem header documents the rejected district-scoped attach draw — contradicts the shipped global street ring and the PR body's own rationale
evidence: `# the user's blessed calm default) with estates clustering within districts` / `# (the growth_groups interplay: the ATTACH family draws from the anchor's` / `# district pool — a cluster never crosses a district boundary).` vs core/growth.odin:512 `// caller draws one index. The ring is GLOBAL (not district-scoped): the` and the PR body: 'a district-scoped DRAW domain was measured and rejected (63% of pool tiles have zero same-district attach-ring neighbors…)'.
detail: The named golden's header — the canonical doc of the behavior it pins — claims a district-scoped attach pool with no cross-district clusters; the implementation draws a GLOBAL ring and clusters can cross Voronoi boundaries. The r2 fix commit ('honest headers (W1/W2)') missed this stale header. Spec required 'document the exact interplay' — this documents the wrong one.
recommended_fix: Rewrite the header to the shipped semantics: ATTACH draws the anchor's global street ring (pool tiles within [min_sep, radius] of a member); districts are label anchors, not draw domains.

title: 'freed at exit' ownership claims are false — map_board_destroy is never called from the app
evidence: app/main.odin:92 `// (loaded once at boot, freed at exit) and shared with the sim + the` and core/map.odin:130-132 `// map_board_destroy — free the board's owned buffers (the caller owns the` / `// board value; call once when the process is done with it — the app frees at` / `// exit, the harness's board cache lives for the process)`. Repo-wide grep for map_board_destroy returns only core/map.odin (definition + load-fail path) and core/map_test.odin — no call in app/ or harness/.
detail: Both comments claim the app frees the board at exit; nothing does. Behaviorally harmless at process exit (fonts leak the same way), but the ownership contract documented in new code is wrong.
recommended_fix: Either call map_board_destroy(&app.board) on the app exit path when board_ok, or correct both comments to 'lives for the process'.

title: map.odin dedupe-cost comment says '719 pool' — the actual 1-in-6 pool is 720 tiles
evidence: `// Linear scan (no map iteration, ODN-10): 37k tiles × 719 pool is` / `// trivial at load.` Mechanical recomputation over data/maps/dublin.json (stride-6 subsample of 224646 spawn_candidates, snap, in-grid filter, dedupe) yields 720 pool tiles and 37441 in-grid render dots; the PR body's own boot line states `app: map = dublin (data/maps/dublin.json, 720 spawn tiles at 1-in-6)`.
detail: Off-by-one stale count in a comment inside the file whose comments are treated as canonical documentation; the code is correct (pool length is computed, not hard-coded).
recommended_fix: Update the comment to '37k tiles × 720 pool' (or drop the counts and reference the boot-time print).
